steps.title: Prepare HEK293T cell culture
steps.instruction: Culture HEK293T cells in DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin in a 182 cm² flask containing 20 ml medium. Maintain cells by aspirating media, washing once with PBS, trypsinizing with 0.05 % trypsin, and replating at a 1/12 dilution in complete DMEM in a 182 cm² flask; split every 3 days. One day before transfection, plate approximately 4 × 10⁶ cells per 182 cm² flask in 18 ml complete DMEM. Use cells that have been in culture ≤4 weeks and never let them reach 100 % confluence.

steps.title: Calcium phosphate transfection for virus production
steps.instruction: Remove all medium from each flask. Add 17 ml fresh DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) containing a final concentration of 25 µM chloroquine to the bottom of the flask, swirl gently and incubate 30–60 min at room temperature. In a 15 ml conical tube, prepare DNA mix: 45 µg HIV GKO plasmid + 25 µg HIV‑1 dual‑tropic envelope plasmid diluted with nuclease‑free H₂O to a total volume of 1.5 ml. Add 1.75 ml 2× HBSS buffer, vortex, then add 220 µl 2 M CaCl₂ dropwise while vortexing (≈45 s). Incubate the DNA‑CaCl₂ mixture at room temperature for 10–30 min. Add the mixture to the bottom of the flask, swirl gently, and culture for 6–8 h at 37 °C. Remove the supernatant, add another 17 ml fresh DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) to the bottom of the flask, and incubate for 48 h at 37 °C to allow viral production.

steps.title: Harvest and clarify viral supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the 48‑h supernatant into a 50 ml Falcon tube. Centrifuge 20 min at 800 × g at room temperature (or 4 °C). Filter the clarified supernatant through a 50 ml centrifuge‑tube filtration unit. Transfer the filtered supernatant into UltraClear centrifuge tubes, ensuring each tube contains at least 34 ml (add media or PBS if needed).

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge viral supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin the UltraClear tubes in an ultracentrifuge for 2 h at 100,000 × g at 4 °C. After the run, carefully pour off the supernatant, dry the inside of the tube as much as possible, and resuspend the viral pellet in 50 µl cold RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) or FBS. Pipet up and down at least 50 times to avoid air bubbles.

steps.title: Resuspend viral pellet and aliquot
steps.instruction: Aliquot the 50 µl resuspended virus into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes and store at –80 °C. Note that concentrated virus can be used fresh or frozen; frozen stocks may require higher input to achieve the same infection rate.

steps.title: Optional: Titer viral stock by p24 assay
steps.instruction: Thaw one aliquot and prepare serial dilutions ranging from 1:10 000 to 1:1 000 000. Perform the FlaQ p24 assay (Gesner et al., 2014) to determine p24 content. Additionally, infect activated CD4⁺ T cells with 4–5 viral dilutions to measure infection rate; aim for ≤15 % total infection (productive + latent).

steps.title: Isolate primary CD4+ T cells from blood
steps.instruction: Obtain fresh blood or leukoreduction chambers (LRC). Transfer to a 50 ml Falcon tube (cut LRC chambers if used). Add 1 800 µl RosetteSep Human CD4⁺ T‑cell enrichment cocktail, incubate 20 min at room temperature, swirling every 5 min. In a new 50 ml tube, add 10 ml Histopaque‑1077. Dilute the sample with an equal volume of PBS containing 2 % FBS, then carefully layer this diluted sample onto the Histopaque. Centrifuge 20 min at 800 × g, room temperature, brake off. Collect the white ring (CD4⁺ T cells) below the plasma layer, transfer to a new 50 ml tube, and wash with PBS + 2 % FBS; centrifuge 3 min at 800 × g and discard supernatant. If the pellet appears red, resuspend in 15 ml cold AKC lysis buffer, incubate 2 min at room temperature, then fill to 50 ml with PBS + 2 % FBS and centrifuge 3 min at 800 × g. Repeat lysis if red persists. Finally, resuspend the CD4⁺ T‑cell pellet in warm RPMI supplemented with 10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep, and 20 U/ml IL‑2. Count cells and culture at 5 × 10⁶ cells/ml (e.g., 250 million cells in a 185 cm² flask). Medium can be changed every 4–5 days; cells remain largely resting.

steps.title: Activate CD4+ T cells with Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Vortex the Dynabeads Human T‑Activator CD3/CD28 vial. Transfer 3.125 ml of beads (1 bead per 2 cells, i.e., half the manufacturer’s recommended amount) to a 15 ml tube. Place the tube on a magnetic rack for 1 min, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the beads in 10 ml of the CD4⁺ T‑cell suspension (5 × 10⁶ cells/ml). Add this bead‑cell mixture to the remaining CD4⁺ T cells. Transfer the whole suspension to an appropriate vessel (e.g., 5 × 10⁶ activated cells per well of a 24‑well plate). Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 3 days; cell aggregates should be visible.

steps.title: Spin‑infect activated CD4+ T cells
steps.instruction: Three days after activation, collect the cells and beads, transfer to 15 ml tubes, and place on a magnet for 1 min. Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 ml tube, then centrifuge the cell‑bead pellet 3 min at room temperature, 800 × g. Discard supernatant and resuspend the 250 million‑cell pellet in RPMI containing the HIV GKO viral preparation at 10 000 ng p24 Gag / ml. Distribute 30 µl of this cell/virus suspension into each well of a 96‑well V‑bottom plate using a multichannel pipette. Centrifuge the plate for 2 h at 800 × g, 32 °C (spin‑infection). Add 100 µl fresh RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) + 20 U/ml IL‑2 to each well, pool the cells, and resuspend in 100 ml fresh RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) + 20 U/ml IL‑2. Transfer the culture to a 182 cm² flask and incubate 4–5 days at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Replace half of the medium every other day by centrifuging the cells (800 × g, 3 min) and adding fresh RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) + 20 U/ml IL‑2.

steps.title: Sort cell populations by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Five days post‑infection, collect cells into 50 ml tubes, centrifuge 3 min at room temperature, 800 × g, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 2 ml FACS buffer. Pass the suspension through a 5 ml 35 µm cell‑strainer cap tube and keep on ice. Prepare labeled 15 ml collection tubes each containing 2 ml FBS on ice. Sort the cells on a FACS Aria II (PE channel for mKO2, FITC for GFP) using an 85 µm nozzle at 4 °C. Collect up to two populations at a time, aiming for ~5 million cells per population; expect 1.5–2.5 million latently infected cells. After sorting, spin the collected cells 3 min at room temperature, 800 × g, resuspend in fresh RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep) + 20 U/ml IL‑2, and distribute equally into a 96‑well V‑bottom plate. For LRA testing, divide the cells equally into five wells (200 µl per well, total resuspension volume 1 ml RPMI).

steps.title: Rest sorted cells overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the sorted cells in the 96‑well plate for 16–24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Treat cells with latency‑reversing agents
steps.instruction: Prepare 2× LRA stock solutions in complete RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % pen/strep, 20 U/ml IL‑2). Remove 100 µl of medium from each well and add 100 µl of the corresponding 2× LRA solution, achieving the desired final concentration. Incubate for 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Stain and analyze cells by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: After the 24‑h drug incubation, discard all medium and wash cells once with FACS buffer. Spin 3 min at room temperature, 800 × g, discard supernatant. Stain with LIVE/DEAD Violet Fixable Dead Cell Stain (1 : 1000 dilution in FACS buffer, 100 µl per well) and incubate 10–15 min on ice in the dark. Wash once with FACS buffer and proceed directly to flow‑cytometry analysis (no fixation with PFA). Use appropriate gating (see Figure 4) on a flow cytometer equipped with FITC, PE, and violet channels (e.g., Aria II, LSRII, or Calibur).
